The canonical spelling of an emoji

Source: R/emoji-catalogue.R
as_emoji_canonical.Rd

as_emoji_canonical() maps each glyph to the one spelling the catalogue marks fully-qualified, so that the bare heart U+2764 and the qualified heart U+2764 U+FE0F become the same string. It is the normalisation every verb in the package applies before a join, exported so a join of your own can apply it too.

Usage

as_emoji_canonical(x)

Arguments

x

A character vector of glyphs.

Value

A character vector the same length as x.

Details

Two spellings of one emoji differ only in the variation selector U+FE0F, and a plain dplyr::left_join() on the glyph treats them as different keys, which silently drops every row whose text holds the other spelling. Canonicalising both sides first is the fix. A glyph the catalogue does not know comes back unchanged, so the function is safe to apply to a whole column, and NA stays NA.

The canonical spelling is a choice of bytes, not of meaning: a skin tone, a gender sign and a ZWJ component are part of the emoji and are kept. Use emoji_identical() to ask whether two glyphs are the same emoji, and how they differ when they are not.

See also

emoji_identical(), emoji_properties().

Examples

as_emoji_canonical(c("\u2764", "\u2764\ufe0f", "\u263a", "not an emoji"))
#> [1] "❤️"            "❤️"            "☺️"            "not an emoji"
